settings.editor:
Have you ever turned on the kitchen sink and been hit with a smell that makes you wonder if something died under the cabinets?

If the odor seems to come from your garbage disposal, you're not imagining it. It's one of the most common plumbing complaints homeowners have, especially during the warmer months when food residue breaks down more quickly.

The frustrating part is that many people clean the disposal, enjoy a day or two of fresh-smelling air, and then the odor comes right back.

That's usually a sign the smell isn't coming from the disposal itself—it's coming from buildup that's been collecting somewhere in the system.

At Petitt Heating & Cooling, we help homeowners across Springfield, Hendersonville, White House, Gallatin, Portland, and surrounding Middle Tennessee communities solve plumbing problems like this every day. In many cases, the fix is simple. In others, a persistent odor can point to a clog or drainage issue that's worth addressing before it becomes a bigger repair.

Here's what causes garbage disposal odors, why they keep returning, and what you can do to get rid of them for good.

settings.title: Quick Answer: Why Does My Garbage Disposal Smell?

settings.editor: A garbage disposal usually smells because food scraps, grease, bacteria, or organic buildup have collected inside the disposal, under the rubber splash guard, or farther down the drain. If the odor keeps coming back after cleaning, it may be caused by buildup in the drain line, dishwasher connection, or a developing clog that requires more than routine cleaning.

settings.title: Why Garbage Disposal Smells Keep Coming Back

settings.editor:
Most homeowners assume the blades are dirty. 

Surprisingly, the blades are rarely the problem. 

Garbage disposals don't actually use sharp blades. They use impellers that grind food against a grinding ring, leaving plenty of places for tiny bits of food, grease, and residue to collect.

Even if the disposal seems clean, odors often linger because buildup remains in places you can't easily see.

Some of the most common hiding spots include:

  • Under the rubber splash guard
  • Inside the disposal chamber
  • The sink drain
  • The dishwasher drain connection
  • The P-trap beneath the sink
Cleaning only one of these areas may temporarily remove the smell without addressing the real source.

settings.title: 1. Food Buildup Under the Splash Guard

settings.editor:
If your garbage disposal smells every time you turn it on, the rubber splash guard is one of the first places to check.

The flexible rubber flaps around the opening are great at preventing food and water from splashing back up the drain. Unfortunately, they also create small folds where tiny bits of food can get trapped.

Over time, that buildup begins to break down, creating the perfect environment for bacteria and unpleasant odors.

The good news is that it's usually an easy fix.

With the disposal turned off, lift the rubber flaps and scrub underneath them with dish soap and a soft brush or sponge. Many homeowners are surprised by how much residue collects there because it's completely hidden from view.

settings.title: 2. Grease and Food Waste Coating the Disposal

settings.editor:
Grease may go down the drain as a liquid, but it doesn't stay that way for long. 

As it cools, it sticks to the inside of the disposal and drain pipes, creating a layer that traps food scraps and allows bacteria to grow. 

Common culprits include:

  • Bacon grease
  • Cooking oils
  • Butter
  • Fat from meat
  • Cream-based sauces
If grease buildup is causing the odor, simply running water won't remove it.

A garbage disposal handles food every day.

Without regular cleaning, naturally occurring bacteria begin feeding on leftover residue inside the disposal and drain.

Those bacteria are what produce many of the unpleasant smells homeowners notice.

This is why masking odors with lemon peels or air fresheners usually doesn't solve the problem for very long.

The bacteria are still there.

Many homeowners don't realize their dishwasher and garbage disposal are connected.

If food or dirty water backs up into that connection, odors can travel right back into the disposal.

You may notice the smell gets worse shortly after running the dishwasher.

If that's happening consistently, the dishwasher drain line or connection may need to be inspected and cleaned.

settings.title: 5. A Partial Drain Clog May Be Trapping Food

settings.editor:
If the odor returns no matter how often you clean the disposal, the problem may actually be farther down the drain.

A partial clog can trap food particles before they fully wash away.

As that debris sits inside the pipe, it begins to decompose, creating odors that rise back through the sink.

Signs this may be the issue include:

  • Slow draining water
  • Gurgling sounds
  • Frequent odors
  • Water backing up into the sink
At that point, cleaning the disposal alone usually isn't enough. The drain may need to be professionally cleaned to remove the buildup that's causing the odor.

settings.title: How to Safely Clean a Smelly Garbage Disposal

settings.editor:
If the odor seems limited to the disposal itself, try these steps:

  1. Turn off the disposal.
  2. Scrub underneath the rubber splash guard.
  3. Flush the disposal with hot water and dish soap.
  4. Grind a small amount of ice to help remove light residue.
  5. Finish by rinsing with plenty of cold water while the disposal runs.

Avoid using harsh chemical drain cleaners.

They often don't remove the buildup causing the odor and can damage plumbing components over time.

settings.title: What Not to Put Down Your Garbage Disposal

settings.editor:
Preventing odors often starts with changing a few kitchen habits.

Avoid putting these items down the disposal:

  • Grease or cooking oil
  • Coffee grounds
  • Eggshells
  • Pasta or rice
  • Fibrous vegetables like celery
  • Bones
  • Fruit pits
These materials either stick to the system or increase the likelihood of clogs.

settings.title: When It's Time to Call a Plumber

settings.editor:
If you've thoroughly cleaned the disposal and the odor continues coming back, it's time to investigate further.

Persistent smells may indicate:

  • A drain clog
  • Grease buildup
  • A blocked vent
  • A plumbing drainage issue
  • A failing garbage disposal
The sooner those problems are identified, the easier they usually are to fix.

settings.title: Don't Let a Bad Smell Turn Into a Bigger Plumbing Problem

settings.editor:
A garbage disposal that smells bad is usually more than just an inconvenience—it's often an early sign that food residue, grease, or a developing clog is building up where it shouldn't.

Many odor problems can be resolved with a thorough cleaning and a few simple maintenance habits. But if the smell keeps coming back, it's worth having the system inspected before a minor issue turns into a more expensive plumbing repair.
